transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-19
- Time: 15:00 UTC (48 minutes)
- Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Rahul Menon (Redwood SE), Jonah Li (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (Head of MLOps), Daniel Ortiz (CTO), Priya Nair (Platform Eng)

Summary: quick renewal/expansion check-in. Customer wants predictable cost, lower tail latency in EU, and a path for data sovereignty for PHI. Redwood to propose commercial options and run perf tests.

[00:00:12] Elena: hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice. quick round — rahul, jonah, you good?
[00:00:18] Rahul: yep, all set. i have the test checklist pulled up.
[00:00:22] Maya: thanks, elena. we appreciate it. scheduled this to make sure we land on numbers by end of month.
[00:00:27] Daniel: yeah, timeline's tight — board wants a commitment before end of Q2.
[00:00:33] Elena: understood. our goal today is to make the tradeoffs explicit: committed capacity size, regions (EU / APAC), and sovereignty path — hosted vs dedicated vs on-prem hybrid.
[00:00:45] Priya: quick note — we have two buckets: de-identified inference that's ok in hosted EU, and PHI flows that need customer-managed keys and strict audit logs, probably on private infra.

[00:00:58] Rahul: okay, so technically we see two parallel paths: 1) expand hosted EU capacity (fast, lower ops), 2) pilot private deployment in EU for PHI (longer lead, more ops). we can also do a mixed model — route PHI to private nodes and everything else to hosted.
[00:01:15] Maya: that mixed routing is what we're leaning to. cost is a big factor though — can you show delta between hosted burst vs reserved dedicated pools?

[00:01:28] Elena: absolutely. we'll prepare two financial scenarios: a 12-month commit with moderate uplift and a 24-month larger commit with more favorable unit pricing. we'll include reserved pool and hybrid on-prem crediting for pilot.

[00:01:40] Daniel: also latency — our European customers expect 60–80ms tail for inference. what's realistic for hosted EU?

[00:01:48] Rahul: realistic is about 40–70ms median for typical seq lengths, but tails can spike 100–200ms on large KV cache misses or cold-model loads. with prefix-KV caching and pinned workers (dedicated) tails tighten to sub-100ms. there's also warm pools and continuous batching configs we can tune.

[00:02:10] Maya: is that with quantized models? we plan to use quant-8 variants in prod.

[00:02:15] Rahul: yes we've benchmarked q4_8 and int8-like variants — they reduce latency ~15–25% on GPU 4090-class or A1-class infer hardware, depending on seq length. caveat: some model ops may degrade quality slightly, so we'll couple that with evals.

[00:02:33] Priya: on the sovereignty side: KMS is a hard ask. we need customer-controlled KMS for the PHI workload, HSM or cloud KMS with separate key material. also audit log retention for 7 years per our policy. can Redwood support that?

[00:02:50] Elena: yes — Redwood Private supports KMS integrations (HSM/KMS) and audit logs. for hosted, we have managed KMS by default, but private deployments let you bring-your-own. i'll prod legal and infra to map exact retention SLAs; jonah will help on the compliance mapping.

[00:03:05] Jonah: i'll pull the SOC2 & FedRAMP adjacency docs, and we can map compliance gaps.

[00:03:12] Daniel: good. another question about routing: do you do smart routing by customer tag? we want to route PHI traffic to private pool automatically.

[00:03:20] Rahul: yes, routing rules support attribute-based routing — you can tag requests and set policy to route by region, latency SLO, or data classification. fallback policies exist if private pool is saturated.

[00:03:35] Maya: when you say fallback — is that automatic? we need to guarantee no PHI leaves private nodes.

[00:03:41] Rahul: fallback is configurable. for PHI, we'd recommend no-fallback to hosted; instead, we provide burst credits or prioritized scaling for your private pool to avoid accidental egress.

[00:03:53] Elena: to be clear, we can set a policy that fails requests if private capacity is exceeded, or queue them — depends on your tolerance.

[00:04:00] Priya: we'll need early-warning alerts on approach to capacity and a predictable scaling plan.

[00:04:06] Rahul: alerting, tracing, and per-route telemetry are available in the Console — token-level cost, per-request latency histograms, and KV cache hit rates. we'll include sample dashboard screenshots in the follow-up.

[00:04:20] Maya: perf tests — we want an apples-to-apples benchmark between our current in-house infra and Redwood hosted EU. can you run a 48-hour perf window?

[00:04:28] Rahul: we can do 24–72 hours. we'll need your QPS pattern and a couple of representative prompts; also sequence length distribution. once we have those, we spin up the test harness and provide logs + a benchmark report.

[00:04:40] Daniel: timeline?

[00:04:42] Elena: if you get us QPS and sample prompts by Friday (2026-05-21), rahul can run a test week of 2026-05-26. results by the following week.

[00:04:52] Maya: yes, we'll extract and share. one more — pricing: does the committed compute credit cover private pilot?

[00:04:58] Elena: typically we model private as a separate line item because there are infra and ops costs. however, for pilots we can structure credits or reduced pilot fees as part of a committed deal. we'll show both line items in the scenarios.

[00:05:10] Priya: ok. legal will also ask about data residency across APAC — we need clarity on region pins and cold storage of logs.

[00:05:17] Jonah: we'll include region pinning specifics and retention options. also note we support regional log export to your SIEM or S3 with bucket-level control.

[00:05:26] Maya: competition — we've talked to x, anthro... uh anthropic and some openai options. price/performance is close; the tie-breaker is the private deployment and the observability features.

[00:05:36] Elena: totally — that's where we focus: predictable unit economics and meaningful observability so platform teams can own SLAs.

[00:05:42] Daniel: any blockers on your side to commit timeline?

[00:05:45] Elena: no blockers — just need QPS, model/prompts, and a decision on commit length. we'll deliver the two pricing scenarios and the pilot playbook.

[00:05:54] Rahul: technical note — for EU private we'll propose a small cluster (2–4 reserved GPUs) to start, with autoscale policies. we'll size it conservatively and tune based on the perf window.

[00:06:06] Priya: for the pilot, can we get an ops runbook? ssh, deploy access, runbooks for incident ops?

[00:06:11] Rahul: yes, we'll provide an on-prem runbook and how to integrate your KMS/HSM — details in the pilot playbook.

[00:06:18] Maya: perfect. then next steps recap?
[00:06:22] Elena: sure — elena: send commercial scenarios and example contract language (by 2026-05-22). rahul: schedule perf window and share test matrix (tentatively 2026-05-26). jonah: compliance doc pack. maya/priya: share QPS and KMS/legal contacts by 2026-05-21.

[00:06:38] Daniel: sounds good.
[00:06:40] Priya: okay thanks — one small note, the audit log retention we asked for 7 years — is that feasible in Private?

[00:06:46] Jonah: yes, retention to your specified S3 bucket or archive is supported; we'll provide the retention config options.

[00:06:53] Elena: great — we'll follow up with a consolidated email and attach the pricing scenarios, bench plan, and pilot playbook.
[00:07:00] Maya: thanks, appreciate it.
[00:07:03] (call wraps up; casual chatter)

Notes on transcript quality:
- Some product names transcribed as "Redwood Private"/"Redwood Console" correctly but occasional mis-hearings: "KV cache" appears as "K V cash" in a few places.
- Speaker overlap detected at 00:01:15 and 00:05:42 causing minor tags to shift.

References / Links mentioned during call:
- Redwood compliance pack (link shared after call)
- Benchmark template (rahul to share)

Recap (single-sentence): Redwood and Praxis Health agreed on a two-track plan: immediate hosted EU capacity uplift with a 12/24-month commercial proposal, and a parallel EU private pilot for PHI workloads with a benchmarking window planned for the week of 2026-05-26.
